title: Kunti Meets Karna
text:
Long before her marriage, while still a girl, Kunti had borne a son to the sun god Surya. Afraid of disgrace, she put the baby in a basket and set him adrift on a river. A charioteer and his wife found him and raised him as their own. They named him Karna.

Karna grew into a great warrior, but because people believed he was a charioteer's son, he was mocked by the princes, and the only one who honored him was Duryodhana. Karna became his loyal friend, and so an enemy of the Pandavas, Kunti's five younger sons.

On the eve of the great war, Kunti went to Karna as he stood praying by the Ganges. She told him the truth: he was her firstborn and the Pandavas were his brothers. She begged him to join them.

Karna answered that she had abandoned him when he most needed a mother, and that Duryodhana had stood by him when no one else would. He would not betray his friend now. But he gave her a promise: he would not kill any of her sons except Arjuna. Whatever happened, she would still have five sons.

In the war, Arjuna killed Karna. Only afterward did the Pandavas learn they had killed their own elder brother.
lesson: Family secrets do not stay small. A truth kept hidden for years can do more harm when it finally comes out than it would have done if told early.
